prompt: Researchers testing a weight-loss program expect men and women to respond differently. They first split the $80$ volunteers into a men's group and a women's group, then randomly assign the program or a control within each group. What is this design called?
hint: Grouping subjects by something you expect to matter, BEFORE randomizing, has a specific name in experiments.

hints.text: Grouping subjects by something you expect to matter, BEFORE randomizing, has a specific name in experiments.
The groups (men, women) are blocks. Random assignment happens separately inside each block.
That is a randomized block design: choice B.

explanation: Sex is expected to affect weight loss, so the researchers block on it: men form one block, women another.
Inside each block, subjects are randomly assigned to the program or the control.
Blocking removes the sex-to-sex variation from the comparison, making the treatment effect easier to see. Choice B. (Stratifying is the sampling cousin of blocking, but this is an experiment.)

alternativeExplanations.title: Why not completely randomized
steps: A completely randomized design would mix everyone together and randomize once.
By chance it might put more women in the program group, muddying the comparison.
Blocking guarantees a fair men-vs-men and women-vs-women comparison.
